meta.title: Finnish A2 Elementary
meta.subtitle: 750 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Finnish → English (see the Finnish, recall the meaning) and English → Finnish (see an English meaning, recall the Finnish). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 750 words of Finnish for an elementary learner, aligned to A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance' — a learner here is able to manage simple, routine exchanges of information on familiar matters — personal and family information, shopping, the local area, work — and to describe in simple terms their background, their surroundings and what they immediately need. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Finnish has an examination graded to these levels (the National Certificates of Language Proficiency, YKI), but no graded word list for it was found published, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 408 of the 750 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — relatives and the people around you, jobs and study, clothes, more food and cooking, the rooms and furniture of a home, the town and its services, travel and holidays, nature, the seasons and the compass, animals, health and the body, feelings and character, free time and sport, telling what happened when, the higher numbers and measures, and the everyday verbs of moving, dressing, cooking and doing — and the other 342 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Finnish, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case of a noun and every form of a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Verbs are given as Finnish dictionaries give them, in the first infinitive (syödä "to eat", puhua "to speak"). The 392 nouns show their plural, their genitive, their partitive and their plural partitive, the forms consonant gradation and stem changes make hard to guess (käsi, kädet, käden, kättä, käsiä), and behind the All forms fold every case in both numbers; the 175 verbs show their "I" and "he, she" forms, their past and their perfect (syödä: syön, syö, söi, on syönyt), and behind the fold the present, the negative, the past, the perfect, the conditional and the imperative by person, and the passive. The Finnish Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters and their sounds. Real example sentences come with 744 of the 750 words, three apiece for 727 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
